A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stereochemical course of the cycloaddition is governed by steric hindrance.

the stereochemistry of the major isoxazolidine is determined by the steric hindrances of the cyclic acetonides and the nitrones, while the stereochemistry of minor products is determined by the stereochemistry of nitrones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stereoselectivity of the cycloaddition is not determined by the chirality of the acetal but by the chirality in the nitrone and the steric hindrances of the acetal.
it is possible to control the stereochemistry of the reaction by choosing an appropriate cyclic acetal and nitrone.

the stereochemistry of the isoxazolidine ring is controlled by the steric hindrances of the nitrile oxide, whereas the stereochemistry of its substituents is determined by the stereochemistry of starting material.
